profile.headline: Principal Software Engineer — Platform & Site Reliability | Terraform · AWS · Kubernetes · Observability | Remote
profile.summary:
I keep large, aging systems running while they change underneath them.

I'm the Principal Engineer for the Registry domain at The Knot Worldwide — all of its services, data, and integrations, including payment, marketplace, and retailer integrations.

What that looks like in practice:

Migrations. I'm leading a live 216M-row system of record off SQL Server to Aurora PostgreSQL, engineered for zero downtime and no refactoring — 6 of 17 production consumer apps needed a one-to-two-line compatibility change. A three-layer parity harness and a reversible DNS cutover are why that number is so low.

Reliability. I define and own SLIs and formal SLO targets — latency, error rate, throughput, queue-draining — segmented by service tier, with synthetic monitors and New Relic → PagerDuty alerting. The Adobe Commerce platform I lead ran 99.98% availability last quarter across ~23M transactions at ~234–244 ms median response. Infrastructure as code. Terraform for Aurora/RDS, networking, DNS, and DMS; shared
composable modules my team reuses; Atlantis for PR-based plan and apply. Monitors ship as code alongside the thing they watch. 

About twenty years on-call, in every role but one, and a senior escalation point today. My habit is to fix the incident, then fix the class of incident — a connection-exhaustion crash on our system of record ended in an API-only data-access posture and Kubernetes internal service routing.

Fully remote since 2017.

Tools: AWS · Terraform · Kubernetes · EKS · Helm · Aurora · RDS · PostgreSQL · MySQL · SQL Server · New Relic · Grafana · Loki · CloudWatch · PagerDuty · GitHub Actions · Jenkins · Atlantis · TypeScript/Node · PHP

positions.title: Principal Software Engineer
positions.description:
Principal Engineer for the Registry domain, storefront (Adobe Commerce + Mirakl), affiliate registry, universal registry.

• Provisioned and operated Aurora, SQL Server, MySQL, MariaDB, and PostgreSQL on AWS RDS as code via
  Terraform, including AWS DMS replication. Day-2 ownership: query-plan analysis and index tuning, connection
  pooling, capacity planning, instance-class selection per workload profile, and cost management.
• Traced a service anomaly to dead-tuple bloat — a count(*) falling back to a parallel sequential scan over
  ~5.3M dead rows (~5.2s). After VACUUM restored the visibility map, the index-only scan took over: ~49ms,
  roughly a 100× speedup.
• Ran an AI agent fleet across 12 production repositories during an EOL infrastructure migration project. 40 PRs merged in 11  days against a 5-year median of 9/month, while PR cycle time dropped from 68h to 40h. More throughput  usually means more review load; my fleet arrived with tests, docs, validation, and visual diagrams making the PRs easier to review and verify. 
• Built local-logs: a Grafana + Loki + Alloy stack with a CLI that gives developers the same unified log
  search locally that they have from New Relic and Sumo Logic in production. Opt-in via container labels,
  inert for anyone who doesn't run it.
• Define and own SLIs and formal SLO targets — response time, queue-draining, latency, error rate,
  throughput — segmented by service tier (customer-facing apps vs. background workers vs. internal), backed
  by synthetic transaction monitors and New Relic → PagerDuty alert conditions. The Adobe Commerce platform I
  lead ran 99.98% availability last quarter at ~234–244 ms median response across ~23M transactions, observed
  on a parameterized New Relic dashboard I built.

positions.title: Lead Software Engineer
positions.description:
Lead Engineer for The Knot Registry Store — the eCommerce platform built over the wedding registry
storefront, including drop-ship fulfillment via Mirakl.

• Ended years of direct database access into the eCommerce system of record after it crashed the platform
  through connection exhaustion. Secured leadership backing, built API parity so
  teams had a real path off, opened the migration tickets on their boards, and moved them to Kubernetes
  internal service routes — which also fixed the latency they (correctly) complained about after the cutover.
  Peer teams with no reporting line to me.

• Ran production incidents end-to-end. A weekend outage cleared every registry synced with Amazon: root cause
  was a legacy hardcoded User-Agent that Amazon's API had begun routing unreliably. Shipped a hotfix, then
  added monitoring to verify the fix held. When a cron engine died silently, I added a heartbeat monitor on
  New Relic wired to PagerDuty — turning a silent failure into a paged one.

• Tuned RDS parameters in Terraform (evaluated with mysqltuner, validated with artillery.io load tests in
  integration and QA before production): read APIs ~15% faster, write endpoints ~65% faster.

• Operated production workloads on Kubernetes — Helm chart development (HPA, External Secrets, deploy-time
  migration jobs, lifecycle hooks, ingress and internal routing), buildah→ECR image builds, and pod-level
  incident debugging across ~20 deployments and 7 cron jobs.
